headline: 英倫樂壇兩則側寫
context: 英國音樂圈本週兩則報導都聚焦幕後故事。翻唱艾美懷絲（Amy Winehouse）等歌手的致敬樂團，正替不景氣的英國 live house 撐起票房，一年替場館進帳數百萬英鎊，但也引發模仿者情緒消耗、是否排擠原創音樂人的討論。另一篇則專訪歌手內特．阿莫斯（Nate Amos，藝名 This Is Lorelei），談他戒除藥物依賴後，如何在新專輯裡找回創作與生活的平靜。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Versions of Amy Winehouse and hundreds of other musicians are generating millions for beleaguered UK venues. But what is the emotional toll for the imitators, and are they pushing out original artists? As peak heatwave sun beams down on to a field in Derbyshire, Amy Winehouse tells the crowd she is in need of hydration – so Robbie Williams fetches her a drink. Elsewhere, members of the public stop the Beastie Boys for selfies, Fred Durst grooves along as Diana Ross covers Al Green, and shirtless teenagers form a circle pit during Korn as a woman sits knitting in a camping chair just behind them. James Brown and Prince turn out to be the same artist – just dressed up in different clothes. These are all scenes from Replika festival last month, which won the Guinness world record for the biggest tribute festival, with 108 acts performing across a very sweaty weekend. The punning deserves an accolade of its own: acts included Catfishing the Bottlemen, Pearl Scam, Wrong Jovi and Iffy Clyro. Continue reading...
sources.title: ‘It’s more than backcombing a beehive!’ How tribute acts got massive – and put the live music scene back in the black

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: The singer-songwriter and Water from Your Eyes guitarist was unstoppably prolific, despite a growing dependence on substances. Now sober, he reflects on his new album and the songs that helped him turn his life round For most of his life, Nate Amos made music just to get through the day. There was plenty of it: dozens of self-produced albums and EPs uploaded – since his This Is Lorelei project launched in 2012 – to what was then a plucky, independent platform called Bandcamp. Now 35, he is perhaps the quintessential Bandcamp artist: part bedroom-pop whiz, part alt-country troubadour, part indie rock rascal with a big, heavy heart. His peers treat him like a lost folk hero from a bygone era. Amos is sitting in the basement of a cafe in Camden Town, north London, cradling an iced matcha; coffee makes him “feel like shit”, he says, and he no longer indulges such foibles. The title of one of those Bandcamp albums, OK N8, is tattooed on his knuckles. A friend inked it a few years ago, soon after Amos got sober. “Exactly when you’re not supposed to be making decisions like getting a tattoo on your hand,” he jokes. His active blue eyes dance around behind a golden-brown fringe and an unruly, woodchip beard. In a tough spot he will swing back in his chair and search for answers that always seem to be hiding beneath the table. But each time he stumbles upon the truth, he looks up with a hungry smile. Continue reading...
sources.title: ‘I know what it’s like to be vulnerable’: musician This Is Lorelei AKA Nate Amos on addiction and finding peace

voice_text: 英國音樂圈這週有兩則幕後故事。翻唱艾美懷絲等歌手的致敬樂團，正替不景氣的英國 live house 撐起票房，一年替場館進帳數百萬英鎊，但也讓人討論，這樣會不會消耗模仿者的情緒，甚至排擠原創音樂人。另一則專訪歌手內特．阿莫斯，他戒除藥物依賴之後，在新專輯裡找回了創作跟生活的平靜。
